description: Nova Ltd. engages in the design, development, production, and sale of process control systems used in the manufacture of semiconductors in Taiwan, the United States, China, Korea, and internationally.
description_full: Nova Ltd. engages in the design, development, production, and sale of process control systems used in the manufacture of semiconductors in Taiwan, the United States, China, Korea, and internationally. The company's product portfolio includes a set of metrology platforms for dimensional, films, and materials and chemical metrology measurements for process control for various semiconductor manufacturing process steps, such as lithography, Etch, chemical mechanical planarization, deposition, electrochemical plating, and advanced packaging. It serves various sectors of the integrated circuit manufacturing industry, including logic, foundry, memory, and packaging sectors, as well as process equipment manufacturers. Nova Ltd. was formerly known as Nova Measuring Instruments Ltd. and changed its name to Nova Ltd. in July 2021. Nova Ltd. was incorporated in 1993 and is headquartered in Rehovot, Israel.

financial_summary: Nova Ltd. is a mid-cap technology business with a $10.0B market cap on $881M of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +16% over the past three years and +19% annually across the full decade, the kind of sustained demand persistence that marks a compounder.
Returns on capital run at 33% against a 12% cost of capital — a 21-point spread that is the clearest signature of an economic moat. Gross margins of 56% confirm genuine pricing power.

The business throws off $218M in free cash flow — roughly 25 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, with adequate 0.95× cash conversion.
On the balance sheet, the balance sheet carries net cash, which is the gold standard: the business never has to make desperate decisions in a bad year.
Shareholder yield is only 0.4%, a thin return of capital, and insider ownership is negligible, so management has little personal stake in the long-term outcome.
